proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a regular conditional experiment given \(E_0\), put \(D=Sd\), and, for any class member, define the proof variable
\[
Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0).
\]
The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\), together with positive definiteness in \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, give
\[
\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D.
\]
Taking traces and then applying Jensen's inequality to the nonnegative variable \(\|Y\|_2^2\) yields
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]=\operatorname{tr}(I_D)=D,
\qquad
D^2\le \mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B.
\tag{1}
\]
The final inequality is exactly \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}.  Hence \(B\ge D^2\) is necessary for nonemptiness; the class is empty if \(B<D^2\).  Notice that strict inequality is not a consequence of nonemptiness.

We next give a causal completion used in every asserted channel.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose the event path in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal Z_+\) contained in the interior of \(([0,1]^d)^S\).  All Bernoulli response probabilities below are kept in a fixed interval \([\eta,1-\eta]\), where \(0<\eta<1/2\), and the corresponding responses take values in \(\{0,B\}\).  For \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), two differentiations of binary relative entropy, whose second derivative is bounded on this interval, give
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le C_\eta v^2.
\tag{2}
\]
Draw event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw bounded historical response paths independently across \((s,i)\), from kernels which may vary with \((s,i)\) but satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_P[Q_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=m_s(X_{st}).
\]
Thus, with \(\varepsilon_{sti}=Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{3}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means equal \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set the observed and historical potential outcomes according to \texttt{ass:consistency} and \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}; make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment and every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  These choices give limited anticipation, no spillovers, event transport, and the two full-design restrictions in \texttt{def:full-design-centered-class}.  Set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  In each construction the donor sample is conditionally iid, independent of the panel, and satisfies the covariance and moment envelopes.  Thus the construction is a regular conditional causal-panel law rather than merely an observed regression experiment.

For every compatible \(B\ge D^2\), the three non-donor channels can use the same common donor marginal.  Conditional on \(E_0\), let \(U\) be uniform on
\[
\{\pm\sqrt D\,e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\qquad Z_j=z_0+U_j,
\]
with the \(U_j\)'s iid and independent of the panel.  Symmetry gives
\[
\mathbb E[U\mid E_0]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E[UU^\top\mid E_0]=I_D,
\qquad
\mathbb E[\|U\|_2^4\mid E_0]=D^2\le B.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), (4) verifies both donor envelopes even at \(B=D^2\).

For the treated channel, put
\[
V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\qquad
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\le c_0\).  A sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\) keeps every event-response probability in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  Change only the treated event-response probability in cohort \(s\) by \(v_s\).  The untreated surfaces and all other observed laws remain fixed.  Absorbing the fixed wealth scale into constants, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (2) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{tr}}}(z_0)|
=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_s n_sv_s^2\le Cc_0^2.
\tag{5}
\]

For the smoothing channel, choose \(s_*\) maximizing
\(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\) and set
\[
b=c_b(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)},
\]
where fixed \(c_b>0\) is small enough that the bump support stays in the interior cube for all positive sample sizes.  Perturb only this cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b),
\tag{6}
\]
where \(\psi\) is a fixed smooth compactly supported bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Use an affine carrier having nonzero covariance-standardized slope when \(\lambda>1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\), scaled within the response, Holder, and two-sided-modulus envelopes.  For \(\delta\le b\), the increment of (6) over a displacement of length \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_1\delta^\kappa\) by Holder continuity (and the derivative bound when \(\lambda>1\)); for \(\delta>b\), boundedness of the bump and \(b^\lambda\le C\delta^\kappa\) gives the same conclusion.  Hence sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves both sides of the local-modulus condition.  Because \(S\) is fixed,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
&=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\\
&\ge c\sum_s\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
\]
Use an independent uniform historical design.  Its probability of meeting the bump support is at most \(Cb^d\).  Conditional product structure, (2), and integration over the design yield
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}\le C.
\tag{8}
\]

For the spacing channel use \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}, whose construction uses the common marginal (4).  It gives
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,\mathrm{sp}},dP_{1,\mathrm{sp}}\}
\ge a_{\mathrm{sp}}>0,
\qquad
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-
\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{9}
\]
Only positive affinity is used.  The rare-active-block probability in that construction may be decreased by a fixed factor, making the affinity exceed any prescribed number below one while retaining the rate in (9).

It remains to construct the donor channel, for which we now impose the fixed strict slack \(B-D^2>0\).  Choose \(0<\xi<D\) so that
\[
D^2+\xi^2<B,
\]
put \(r_-=(D-\xi)^{1/2}\) and \(r_+=(D+\xi)^{1/2}\), and choose two interior centers
\[
z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\mu e_1,
\qquad \mu=c_2N^{-1/2}.
\]
The direction \(e_1\) is chosen inside one cohort block.  Use the common finite support
\[
\mathcal A=\{z^{(0)}\pm r_-e_k, z^{(0)}\pm r_+e_k:1\le k\le D\}.
\]
Under law zero, give every atom probability \(1/(4D)\).  Its mean is \(z^{(0)}\), covariance is \(I_D\), and its standardized fourth moment is
\[
\frac{r_-^4+r_+^4}{2}=D^2+\xi^2<B.
\tag{10}
\]
Under law one leave all probabilities except the four atoms in direction \(e_1\) unchanged.  With
\[
a_N=\frac{\mu}{2r_-},
\qquad b_N=\frac{\mu^2}{2\xi},
\]
replace the probabilities at \(z^{(0)}+r_-e_1\), \(z^{(0)}-r_-e_1\), \(z^{(0)}+r_+e_1\), and \(z^{(0)}-r_+e_1\), respectively, by
\[
\frac1{4D}-\frac{b_N}{2}+a_N,
\quad
\frac1{4D}-\frac{b_N}{2}-a_N,
\quad
\frac1{4D}+\frac{b_N}{2},
\quad
\frac1{4D}+\frac{b_N}{2}.
\tag{11}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\), depending on the fixed slack through \(\xi\), all probabilities in (11) are positive for every \(N\).  They sum to their baseline total.  Direct calculation gives
\[
\mathbb E_1[Z_j-z^{(0)}]=2a_Nr_-e_1=\mu e_1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_1[(Z_j-z^{(0)})(Z_j-z^{(0)})^\top]
=I_D+b_N(r_+^2-r_-^2)e_1e_1^\top
=I_D+\mu^2e_1e_1^\top.
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_1 Z_j=z^{(1)}\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_1(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_D\), exactly.  The standardized fourth moment is a continuous function of the finite probability vector and of \(\mu\); by (10), the fixed strict slack permits a further reduction of \(c_2\) such that it remains below \(B\) under both laws.  This is the only point where \(B>D^2\), rather than mere compatibility, is used.

Since the baseline probabilities are bounded below and the perturbations in (11) are \(O(\mu)\), Taylor's formula for the finite probability-vector likelihood gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN(a_N^2+b_N^2)
\le CN\mu^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{12}
\]
For \(\kappa=1\), choose the weighted regression carrier to have nonzero linear slope in direction \(e_1\).  For \(0<\kappa=\lambda<1\), in the selected cohort use
\[
x\longmapsto c_3+c_4|e_1^\top(x-z^{(0)})|^\lambda
+c_5|e_1^\top(x-z^{(1)})|^\lambda,
\qquad c_4,c_5>0,quad c_4\ne c_5.
\tag{13}
\]
Fixed rescaling places (13) inside the response and Holder envelopes.  At \(z^{(0)}\), displacement in the direction away from \(z^{(1)}\) increases both cusp terms; at \(z^{(1)}\), displacement in the opposite outward direction does the same.  The upper Holder inequality controls every displacement.  Thus the two-sided modulus holds at both centers, while evaluation at the centers gives
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_s^{(1)})-m_s(z_s^{(0)})\}\right|
\ge c\mu^\kappa=cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{14}
\]
Keep the historical observed law, the common regression surface, and the observed event mean fixed across the two donor laws.  Under law \(\ell\), complete untreated event outcomes with cohort means \(m_s(z_s^{(\ell)})\).  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (14) into squared target separation at least \(cN^{-\kappa}=cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For the three bounded-divergence channels, the elementary inequality
\[
\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le\{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2\}^{1/2}
\]
follows by applying data processing to the set \(\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\) and bounding the resulting binary relative entropy by twice squared probability difference.  Hence
\[
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
=1-\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\ge1-\{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2\}^{1/2}.
\tag{15}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (15) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and, only under strict slack, donor pairs; (9) handles spacing.  The chosen query belongs to \(\mathcal Z_+\) with conditional probability one.  Equations (2)--(15), the causal completion following (3), and the channelwise design, smoothness, donor, and modulus checks prove all four assertions when \(B>D^2\).  When \(B=D^2\), equations (4)--(9) prove exactly the asserted treated, smoothing, and spacing claims, without a donor converse.

Put \(D=Sd\).  For any member of the class, define \(Y=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_1-z_0)\).  The definitions of \(z_0\) and \(\Sigma\) and \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity} imply \(\mathbb E_P[YY^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Therefore, by taking traces, applying Jensen's inequality, and then using \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment},
\[
D^2=\{\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^2\mid E_0]\}^2
\le\mathbb E_P[\|Y\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le B.
\]
Thus \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class.  Fix henceforth \(B\ge D^2\), an interior query, and one cohort having fixed positive weight; hold all remaining cohorts fixed across the two laws.  For sufficiently small fixed \(c_p,c_L>0\), let
\[
L_T=\lfloor c_L\log(T\vee2)\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=c_p\frac{L_T}{T},
\]
where \(c_L|\log\rho_0|<1\).  Since \(p_T\asymp(\log T)/T\) whereas \(\rho_0^{L_T}\asymp T^{-c_L|\log\rho_0|}\), reducing \(c_p\) gives
\[
2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
\tag{16}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Let \(A_T\) be a Euclidean ball centered at the selected cohort block of \(z_0\), contained in \([0,1]^d\), and having Lebesgue measure \(p_T\).  Its radius satisfies
\[
h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}.
\tag{17}
\]

Partition the calendar into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently across blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw the selected cohort's design points independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  At each time the marginal density equals
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\tag{18}
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:design-density} holds because \(c_X\le1\le C_X\).  At lags at least \(L_T\), the relevant sigma-fields use independent block variables.  At smaller lags, only one shared block can create dependence.  Expanding the two-component mixture bounds its absolute-regularity distance from the product law by \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Since \(\rho_0^\ell\ge\rho_0^{L_T-1}\) for \(1\le\ell<L_T\), (16) implies
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)
\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}<L_T,\\
0,&\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\ge L_T,
\end{cases}
\le\beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}}.
\tag{19}
\]
This is precisely the design-only mixing condition.

Choose a bounded Holder carrier \(g\) lying in the interior of the response range.  Give it a nonzero affine component at \(z_0\) if \(\lambda>1\), and an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp there if \(0<\lambda\le1\); scale it inside the maintained two-sided modulus envelope.  With a fixed smooth bump \(\psi\), supported on the unit ball and satisfying \(\psi(0)=1\), put
\[
m_0(x)=g(x),
\qquad
m_1(x)=g(x)+c_bh_T^\lambda
\psi\left(\frac{x-z_0}{h_T}\right).
\tag{20}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_b\), both surfaces remain in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and in the response interior.  If \(\lambda>1\), the bump increment over displacement \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta\le h_T\), and at most \(Cc_bh_T^\lambda\le Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta>h_T\); it therefore cannot cancel the carrier's affine lower modulus.  If \(0<\lambda\le1\), its increment is at most \(Cc_b\delta^\lambda\), so it cannot cancel the cusp lower modulus when \(c_b\) is small.  The Holder upper bound gives the upper modulus.  Thus both laws satisfy \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Conditional on the complete design, draw bounded historical response paths independently across units from kernels having mean \(m_\ell(X_{st})\); kernels may vary by unit.  Draw bounded event outcomes independently of the design with a common mean under both laws, and complete untreated event potential outcomes so their cohort-average means are \(m_\ell(z_0)\).  Then
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{21}
\]
For the donors use, under both laws, iid copies of
\[
Z_j=z_0+U_j,
\qquad
U_j\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{\pm\sqrt D\,e_k:1\le k\le D\},
\]
independently of the panel.  The calculation in (4) gives \(\Sigma=I_D\) and standardized fourth moment exactly \(D^2\le B\).  In particular, this donor completion remains valid at \(B=D^2\) and carries no information distinguishing the two spacing laws.  Take exact historical coordinates.  Define the potential outcomes by consistency, make historical potential outcomes invariant to event treatment, and make all potential outcomes invariant to other units' assignments.  Equations (18)--(21), the common donor calculation, and these completions verify every member property of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).

Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that no calendar block is active.  Since the number of blocks is \(T/L_T+O(1)\),
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{T/L_T+O(1)}\longrightarrow e^{-c_p}>0.
\tag{22}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), every selected-cohort design point lies outside \(A_T\), where the two surfaces in (20) agree.  The complete observed-data laws therefore coincide on this event, so
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\tag{23}
\]
The observed event mean is common, whereas event transport changes the untreated event mean of the selected cohort by \(c_bh_T^\lambda\).  The identification formula in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and (17) give
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|
\ge ch_T^\lambda
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{24}
\]
For the finitely many \(T\) preceding (16), use a fixed interior ball and two sufficiently close bounded response kernels with positive affinity and fixed nonzero target separation; decreasing the common constant makes (23)--(24) valid for all positive \(T\).

For any estimator, the two events on which its error from the respective target is at least half the separation cover the sample space.  Integrating against the overlap measure in (23) yields conditional squared risk at least \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).  Reducing \(c_p\) makes (23) exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some \(a_0>0\).  A conditionally honest interval covers both target values on overlap measure at least \(a_0\), and on that event its length is at least the separation in (24).  Its worst-case conditional expected length is therefore at least \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\).  This proves the claim for every compatible envelope without an anti-clustering premise.

The compatibility calculation (1) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} proves that the class is empty for \(B<D^2\).  Suppose first that \(B>D^2\).  For a channel \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{don}\}\), take \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) from that lemma, write their conditional target values as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and set \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Their conditional testing affinity is at least a fixed \(a_q>0\), and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\).  For any observed-data estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E'_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E'_1=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space by the triangle inequality.  Integration against the overlap measure gives
\[
P_{0,q}(E'_0\mid E_0)+P_{1,q}(E'_1\mid E_0)\ge a_q,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{a_q\Delta_q^2}{8}\ge cR_q.
\tag{25}
\]
Maximizing over all four channels and using \(R_{\star,\beta}=\max_qR_q\) proves the strict-slack lower bound.  The donor-channel affinity, and hence its lower-bound constant, may depend on \(B-D^2\), exactly as stated.  When \(B=D^2\), the boundary part of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} supplies (25) only for \(q\in\{\mathrm{tr},\mathrm{sm},\mathrm{sp}\}\).  Maximizing over precisely those channels proves the stated three-channel lower bound and makes no donor converse.

The upper bound is common to both nonempty regimes.  Let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,\ t\le T\}
\]
and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On successful fits, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the linear representation in \texttt{def:honest-interval} give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{26}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{hist}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\pi_s
\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{LP}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\left\{\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})
-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right\},
\]
and
\[
B_{\mathrm{don}}=
\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums under this conditioning, and donor independence permits the donor sample to be adjoined.  Conditional cross-unit independence and bounded response ranges imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{27}
\]
Treating one unit's entire response history as one cluster and applying \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} similarly gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{28}
\]
No temporal outcome restriction or identical response law is used.

Let \(C_K\) bound the Euclidean radius of the support of \(K\).  Whenever \(w_{st}>0\), \(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2\le C_Kh_s\).  Polynomial reproduction, the Holder Taylor remainder, and the deterministic absolute-weight bound yield
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz and \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\), first conditional on \(\widetilde z_s\) and then integrated over donors,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{29}
\]
because \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\).

For donor control define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
Conditional donor replication gives independent mean-zero vectors with \(\mathbb E_P[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), all terms containing a singleton sample index vanish.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E_P[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2^4\mid E_0]\le CN^{-2}\).  Euclidean projection onto the cube cannot increase distance from \(z_0\), and ellipticity gives
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\tag{31}
\]
On the event where the left side is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local-modulus inequality bounds \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|^2\) by a constant times that norm to power \(2\kappa\).  Lyapunov's inequality and (30) give expectation at most \(CN^{-\kappa}\).  On the complement, \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le B\), while Markov's inequality and (30) bound its probability by \(O(N^{-2})\).  Hence
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{32}
\]
This argument uses only the upper fourth-moment premise and is valid at equality \(B=D^2\).

Every successful intercept satisfies
\[
|\widehat m_s|\le B\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2},
\]
and a failed intercept contribution is zero.  The squared estimation error is therefore uniformly bounded on the bad sample.  The bad-sample probability in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} makes its contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the asserted arrays.  Combining (26)--(32) with \((x_1+x_2+x_3+x_4)^2\le4\sum_{j=1}^{4}x_j^2\) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{33}
\]
Because \(\widehat\tau\) is one observed-data estimator and does not depend on unknown \(\Sigma\), (33) also upper-bounds the minimax infimum.  Combining it with the appropriate strict-slack or boundary lower argument proves every displayed bracket.

The compatibility calculation (1) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} shows that \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class.  Fix a compatible envelope \(B\ge D^2\), let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,\ t\le T\},
\]
and condition first on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On each successful fit, polynomial reproduction from \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control}, applied to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\), gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{34}
\]
After cohort weighting, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the historical unit-cluster variables
\[
\mathsf H_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} and donor independence give
\[
\mathbb E_P[\mathsf H_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]=0.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables independent over \((s,i)\) under this conditioning.  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(\mathsf H_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|a_{sti}|.
\]
If a conditionally centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its exponential moment by the endpoint mixture with the same mean; differentiating the logarithm of that two-point mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{35}
\]
Multiplying (35) over independent unit clusters, applying exponential Markov inequality, optimizing over \(v>0\), and repeating for \(-U\) yield
\[
P_P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf H_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{36}
\]
Thus each unit's full calendar history is one bounded cluster; no within-unit temporal restriction is used.

Similarly define
\[
\mathsf E_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(\mathsf E_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence preserves centering after donors are adjoined, and cross-unit independence gives conditional independence.  Their conditional range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same calculation gives
\[
P_P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf E_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{37}
\]
A union bound combines (36)--(37), without requiring independence between one unit's historical path and event outcome.

For donor calibration define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
The conditional fourth-moment expansion in (30) gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\tag{38}
\]
Define the proof event \(\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}\).  Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{39}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]^{Sd}\) cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), because \(z_0\) lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds therefore give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_N/\sqrt N
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{40}
\]
On the good event of \texttt{def:honest-interval}, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\).  The upper half of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (40) imply
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{41}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) denote the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j))\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), the fallback interval is \([-B,B]\).  Every potential-outcome contrast has conditional mean in \([-B,B]\), and the positive cohort weights sum to one, so \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) deterministically.  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (34), and (41) decompose the estimation error into the event fluctuation, historical fluctuation, and two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Thus noncoverage implies failure of (36) or (37).  Iterated conditioning gives, for every positive sample size,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P_P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{42}
\]
No selector-tail probability enters (42), so coverage is exact and finite-sample for every compatible envelope, including \(B=D^2\).

For expected length, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives on every successful fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{43}
\]
The support of \(K\) and the same deterministic weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(\lambda\), conditionally on the projected donor center, and use Cauchy--Schwarz across the fixed cohorts.  Then
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{44}
\]
Since \(D,B,\alpha\) are fixed, (38) implies \(q_N\le C\), and hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{45}
\]
The selector lemma gives \(P_P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the asserted arrays.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), and \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on \(\mathcal G\).  Equations (43)--(45) therefore prove, for either compatible regime with its independently quantified upper constant,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{46}
\]

For the strict-slack lower bound, choose the fixed perturbation constants in the four channels of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so that every affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some fixed \(a_0>0\).  For the three Kullback--Leibler-controlled channels this follows by taking their perturbations sufficiently small in (15); in the donor channel the permissible constants may depend on \(B-D^2\).  For spacing it follows by decreasing the rare-block constant.  Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest, let \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) be a channel pair's targets, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) be the conditional overlap measure.  Uniform conditional honesty gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\mid E_0\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\mid E_0\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Consequently
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{48}
\]
Maximizing (48) over all four channels gives the strict-slack lower bound \(c_{\alpha,>}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  At \(B=D^2\), apply the same argument only to the treated, smoothing, and spacing pairs supplied at the boundary by \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}; maximizing over those three channels gives
\[
c_{\alpha,=}\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}^{1/2},
\]
without a donor-channel claim.  If an interval sequence is only uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest, then for each \(\epsilon>0\) both noncoverage probabilities are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Choosing \(\epsilon<a_0/4\) replaces the final bound in (47) by at least \(a_0/2\), proving the same rates.  Equations (42), (46), and (48), with the stated case split, establish every assertion.

prose_updates.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. Consistency and cohort-average event transport identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw local-polynomial estimator is exactly a cohort-weighted event coefficient. With \(D=Sd\), nonemptiness requires \(B\ge D^2\). For every fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), matching bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\); for every fixed otherwise nonempty class with \(B=D^2\), exact coverage and the same four-term upper bounds remain valid, while the universal lower bound contains only treated, smoothing, and log-spacing channels. The feasible construction projects the full independent donor mean once, uses one normalized-shape local-polynomial fit per cohort, and combines bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding radii with exact Holder--Taylor and donor-modulus allowances. The proposed interval is conditionally honest in every finite sample throughout the compatible regime.

project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact cohortwise weighted-panel coefficient representation, exact finite-sample conditional coverage over every compatible envelope, and matching risk and honest-length frontiers for each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\). For each fixed otherwise nonempty class at \(B=D^2\), the estimator and interval upper bounds persist and the proved converse retains exactly the treated, smoothing, and log-spacing channels. A normalized Gram-shape selector under design-only geometric beta mixing, full-data bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding calibration, an exact Taylor allowance, full-sample covariance-standardized donor control, and channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish the result without donor splitting, sequential overlap, a dense-site condition, an upper local-mass condition, or identical unit response laws.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and standardized fourth-moment envelope \(B\); with \(D=Sd\), these conditions can define a nonempty class only when \(B\ge D^2\). Historical training coordinates are exact. The full donor mean is projected once onto the proxy cube and feeds one log-adjusted local-polynomial fit per cohort, selected by normalized Gram shape. The finite-sample conditionally honest interval uses the resulting full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event bounded-cluster Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and one full-sample donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared observable bad sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and explain why compounded buy-and-hold wealth requires more than linear return matching. Barber and Lyon (1997) and Mitchell and Stafford (2000) likewise motivate attention to dependence and compounding in long-horizon returns. Matching only marginal or mean return paths generally discards within-path dependence needed for compounded wealth; here that observation is motivation, not a theorem and not an observational-equivalence claim under the maintained full wealth panel. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates and a sparse-to-dense decomposition, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) analyze generated coordinates attached to every training observation, Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) analyze replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution, and Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study local-polynomial regression evaluated at a sample-split estimated strongly convex minimizer. Those experiments differ from the exact historical coordinates and single generated event query here. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and beta-mixing block-coupling template; here dependence is imposed only on the historical design. Chen and Christensen (2015) provide weak-dependence Gram-matrix control for higher-order sieve regression. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) provide the ordered-modulus language for honest expected length. Ferman (2021) supplies the many-period--many-control motivation for arbitrary relative growth, and Shi et al. (2026) identify synthetic controls through predetermined donor proxies without deriving the generated-proxy minimax frontier. The present proof adds one full-donor center, heterogeneous bounded unit-response clusters with a common conditional mean, exact finite-sample conditional coverage, an explicit rare-block spacing witness, and the donor-envelope boundary qualification.
prose_updates.interpretation: For every integer \(T\ge3\), the replicated-smoothing term obeys \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), where \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\). Hence \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\). For each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), all three active components have matching lower witnesses: the oracle region has \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta})\), the generated-proxy region reverses that relation, and the boundary equates the two. For each fixed otherwise nonempty class at \(B=D^2\), the same upper phase map remains valid but a universal donor lower witness is not asserted, so only the treated and log-spacing active components are universally matched. The sole donor elbow in the upper rate and strict-slack frontier is \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\). The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball or anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality. The risk and honest-length results additionally use the two explicit full-design mean-stability and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence. Geometric beta mixing is required only for the historical design, and bounded unit response paths may otherwise be arbitrarily dependent over time and heterogeneous across units subject to their common conditional mean. Nonemptiness of the donor conditions requires \(B\ge D^2\). The universal donor converse uses fixed strict slack \(B-D^2>0\); at equality only the three non-donor lower channels are proved. The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass. The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp minimax constants.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of event-transport identification, the exact full-donor FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, a log-adjusted selector bound under design-only geometric beta mixing, a positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, compatible-envelope causal-panel lower embeddings, a conditional-risk frontier, and an exact finite-sample conditionally honest interval. For each fixed nonempty class with \(B>D^2\), four lower channels match the risk and expected-length upper rates, with constants allowed to depend on the fixed slack. For each fixed otherwise nonempty class at \(B=D^2\), exact coverage and upper bounds remain, and the proved lower frontier contains treated, smoothing, and spacing channels but no universal donor converse; \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class. Historical and event unit response laws may be heterogeneous and each unit's calendar history is treated as one bounded cluster. No donor splitting, covariance estimation, response-variance lower bound, sequential overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, studentization, or temporal-outcome mixing condition is used. The mean-return dependence point retained in Related Work is motivation only, not an observational-equivalence theorem for the maintained full panel.
